chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Madaini, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about al-fuqqa' (a fermented drink), so he said: 'It is wine.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْفُقَّاعِ: A fermented drink, specifically from barley or wheat, often cited in fiqh texts regarding intoxicants.
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: Wine or intoxicant; the primary category for forbidden drinks in Islamic law.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of al-fuqqa' in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Ammar ibn Musa queries Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding 'al-fuqqa'', a specific fermented drink known in pre-Islamic and early Islamic contexts. The Imam’s definitive classification of it as 'khamr' (wine) underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that any beverage causing intoxication, regardless of its specific name or preparation method, falls under the prohibition of *khamr*. This ruling highlights the emphasis on the substance's effect rather than its etymology, reinforcing the broader Quranic mandate against intoxicants.
